sar.narrative: This suspicious activity report details an organized card-not-present fraud scheme affecting customer C05061 and payment card C05061-K1, along with connected cards C07212-K2 and C11543-K2. Between January 12, 2017, and January 14, 2017, three unauthorized online product-C transactions totaling $2,189.02 were charged to card C05061-K1. The unauthorized activity comprised transaction 3660106 for $850.28 on January 12, transaction 3660107 for $890.79 on January 13, and transaction 3660108 for $447.95 on January 14. All transactions occurred in the online channel and were routed through billing regions 492 and 264 utilizing devices identified as new to the account. Transactions 3660106 and 3660108 were conducted via device D009708 with the profile RCT6303W87M7 Build/MRA58K on Windows 7 with Internet Explorer 11.0 desktop. Transaction 3660107 was conducted via device D009709 with the profile RCT6303W87M7 Build/MRA58K on Windows 10 with Internet Explorer 11.0 tablet. Both devices connected through an anonymous IP proxy to obfuscate the perpetrator's origin and identity. The abrupt high-value product-C charges completely deviated from the cardholder's historical profile, which showed zero product-C transactions over the prior sixty days. Graph analytics identified an identical attack pattern occurring simultaneously across cards C07212-K2 and C11543-K2, which each suffered multiple high-value product-C charges from new devices behind proxies. Furthermore, peer card C07212-K2 is linked to fraud ring 34603052 with nineteen confirmed fraud closed cases. The bank has blocked card C05061-K1, placed connected cards on automated monitoring, and submitted this report regarding the coordinated $2,189.02 fraud episode.

answer.stop_reason: The investigation concluded under policy section 6 because the fraud probability reached 0.885, surpassing the decisive threshold of 0.85 supported by multiple independent evidence bases including anomalous cardholder behavior, proxy-masked new devices, and cross-card links to known fraud ring members, meaning further investigative steps would not alter the decision.

passages.section: Section 3a. A case is not a report
passages.text: Section 3a. A case is not a report. Two different things, and the agent produces both. **A case** (`CREATE_CASE`) is the bank's internal record of an investigation. Open one whenever fraud probability reaches 0.30, whenever you request evidence, or whenever a customer disputes a charge. A case can be closed as fraud or as legitimate. It can be updated when new evidence arrives. It should be written into the graph so later investigations can find it: a case that names a merchant or a device becomes evidence for the next analyst. **A suspicious activity report** (`FILE_REPORT`) is a regulatory filing sent outside the bank. File one when fraud is confirmed or strongly suspected **and** at least one of these holds: exposure exceeds $1,000; the activity connects to a shared device profile, a shared region cluster, or another customer's fraud; the pattern is coordinated or undocumented (rule R9). A report always has a case behind it. Most cases never need a report. The report narrative must stand on its own: who, what, when, where, how, and why it is suspicious. Deciding correctly between ""case only"" and ""case plus report"" is part of the next-best-action score.

Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

assessment.reasoning: The alert concerns an analyst request investigating multiple cards suffering losses this month without an obvious shared device. On card C05061-K1, flagged transaction 3660108 is part of an abrupt run of three high-value online product-C transactions (3660106, 3660107, 3660108) totaling $2,189.02 between 2017-01-12 and 2017-01-14. All three transactions originated from new devices (D009708 and D009709) operating behind an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS). Prior to this burst, card C05061-K1 had negligible product-C activity (2 out of 119 prior transactions). Furthermore, scheme peer analysis identifies an identical attack signature across two other cards during the same window: C07212-K2 (transactions 3660115, 3660116 via D009707 behind proxy) and C11543-K2 (transactions 3660122, 3660123, 3660124 via D009706 behind proxy). Card C07212-K2 belongs to ring 34603052 and has extensive confirmed fraud history (CC-0045, etc.), confirming this coordinated multi-card campaign using disposable devices behind anonymous proxies. This constitutes card-not-present fraud using new devices behind proxies.
